messages:
incident-bot: Pager: inferpool-eu-west-1: node NotReady spike (multiple nodes) affecting inference-pool-usw-eu routing. Alert level: paged oncall.
alyssa: oncall here, seeing the page. anyone oncall in eu?
ben: i'm awake, joining. what's the scope?
incident-bot: Alert details: 18 nodes transitioned to NotReady within 4m. Kubernetes events show kubelet restarts and container OOM on several GPU pods.
chris: I can grab cluster logs and node events. starting `kubectl get nodes --selector=inference-pool=eu -o wide`
sasha: I see repeated kubelet restarts on node-infer-03 and node-infer-07. dmesg shows 'oom_kill' and 'GPU-Driver error: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILURE'.
dana: dashboards: p95 latency for eu model routes up from 180ms -> 420ms. 5xx rate for hosted API in eu region increased to 6.8%. customers hitting timeouts.
ben: running quick health check on pods:```shell
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=eu -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
```
ben: several pods show high restart counts and STATUS CrashLoopBackOff. logs show oom on runtime-worker and then kernel messages about GPU abort.
chris: putting node-infer-03 in cordon to stop scheduling more work: `kubectl cordon node-infer-03`
sasha: cordoned. starting drain with eviction limits (grace 60s):```shell
kubectl drain node-infer-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
infra-bot: Autoscaler suggestion: add 3 spot-capacity nodes to eu cluster to absorb load. Command: `scale-nodegroup eu-infer-workers +3`
dana: agree — we should scale up and also activate fallback routing to the cheaper, lower-latency dedicated pool in us-west for non-EU customers. For EU customers, enable degraded-mode: reduce batch size to lower memory pressure.
ben: applied scale up (infra-bot: nodegroup scale initiated). also patched infer-deployment to reduce maxBatchSize from 64 -> 32 for eu route: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/infer-deployment MAX_BATCH=32`
chris: i'm pulling kubelet journal on node-infer-03: `journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso --since "10 minutes ago"` shows repeated `Segmentation fault` around the time of GPU driver upgrade.
alyssa: was there a driver roll last night? any node image changes?
sasha: config history shows a rolling driver update 2h ago targeting a subset of nodes; node-infer-03 had an out-of-band kernel update queued. suspect mismatch between driver/kernel -> GPU aborts -> OOM during pod restart loops.
dana: customer impact note: routing shows 1200 requests failed in last 10m for accounts in EU-APAC; CS alerted for high priority customers. adding to incident ticket.
ben: created fallback route: `route-manager promote inferpool-eu-fallback` — traffic shifted 30% to fallback models, decreasing errors. metrics are stabilizing slowly.
chris: for immediate remediation, recommend: 1) cordon/drain flaky nodes (done for 03), 2) roll back driver to previous stable on affected nodes, 3) scale up nodes until rollback completes. I'll start driver rollback playbook.
infra-bot: rollback job queued: playbook/driver-rollback-eu started by chris. ETA ~14m.
dana: posting to #incidents with summary and customer impact. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/eu/inference/alerts/1723456789
alyssa: i need a formal handoff in 15m to night oncall. chris, ben — are you staying for the rollback?
ben: staying until nodes stable, then handoff ok.
chris: i'll own the rollback and post status updates.
deploy-bot: Notice: infer-deployment autoscaling: added 3 nodes, pods rescheduled.
sasha: after cordon/drain of 03 and 07, pods moved to new nodes, some still crash due to driver mismatch; rollback in progress.
dana: monitoring: error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 2.1% after traffic shift and scaling. latency p95 trending down.
alyssa: created incident ticket INC-2024-7234 (Sev2) with initial timeline and actions. linking runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/infer/node-flap-oom
ben: note for postmortem: investigate driver roll orchestration — why two nodes received kernel/drivers out-of-sync. add canary guard.
chris: rollback completed on nodes 03/07/11. kubelet stable, pods recovered. marking nodes uncordon in batches. `kubectl uncordon node-infer-03`
sasha: uncordoned. pods running READY.
dana: final check: 5xxs back to baseline (0.6%), p95 ~190ms.
alyssa: handoff: i'm passing to night oncall `chris` in 10m. keep monitoring cloudwatch alerts and the incident page.
chris: acknowledged. will monitor for 1h and escalate if relapse.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-7234 acknowledged: status = mitigated, severity = Sev2 -> monitoring.
alyssa: thanks team :heart: closing thread, will draft postmortem tomorrow.
ben: good job everyone.
